title: Search Bar Design System
summary: This lesson breaks down search as a five-part system rather than a single input field. It covers optimizing placeholders, recent searches, autocomplete ranking, keyboard accessibility, and zero-results recovery.

transcript.text: Search is a system. Five parts. Most apps skip them.
Placeholder copy is your first onboarding. 'Search' tells nothing. 'Search by name, SKU, or brand' tells everything.
Empty state isn't empty. Recent searches load when users focus. One click fills the bar. Friction drops to zero.
Autocomplete ranks results by clicks, not alphabet. Each option shows a category badge. Three results beat ten.
Arrow keys navigate results. Enter selects, Escape closes. The focus ring must stay visible.
Zero results shouldn't be a dead end. Suggest alternatives: popular searches or category jumps. Bad empty states lose users at the worst moment.
Follow for more UI systems. Save this for your next search bar. The best UI feels invisible until it fails.
